title: Compassion Benchmark Daily Briefing -- July 23, 2026
headline: A proposed lower score for Guinea-Bissau follows a 2025 coup, but the change has not been applied.
summary: Fifteen governments, cities, and companies were reviewed overnight. Thirteen scores held within the benchmark's five-point confirmation range. A proposed lower score for Guinea-Bissau, following a November 2025 military coup, has not been applied; the country's published score remains 20.3 out of 100. A separate proposal for Becton Dickinson, the medical device maker, fixes a math error in how its stored scores add up to its public score. That is bookkeeping, not a finding about the company's conduct, and Becton Dickinson stays in the Functional band either way. The Democratic Republic of the Congo's near-zero score held as its Ebola outbreak passed 1,000 deaths in under ten weeks, the fastest pace on record. Russia, Israel, and Iran all held at or near the benchmark's floor on their own conduct, while Ukraine and Palestine held steady despite rising casualties, because those casualties are inflicted by others, not by their own governments. Flooding in Ahmedabad, India, and a New York lawsuit against DuPont over long-lasting "forever chemicals" both confirmed existing low scores rather than changing them.

pipeline.queueHandling: Two findings were documented this cycle -- a coup-era country downgrade and a company data correction -- and both remain unapplied; the published scores stand at 20.3 for Guinea-Bissau and 54.1 for Becton Dickinson.

topSignals.title: A Proposed Downgrade for Guinea-Bissau Follows a Military Coup, but the Score Has Not Changed
topSignals.whyItMatters: A country's government seized power by force and jailed its opposition leader. A lower score reflecting that has been proposed, but it has not taken effect, so the public score is unchanged for now.
topSignals.description: Guinea-Bissau's published score remains 20.3 out of 100, in the Developing band. On November 23-26, 2025, the country's Military High Command seized power before election results were announced, and the country was suspended from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), the African Union, and the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP). Freedom House cut Guinea-Bissau's separate freedom score by 8 points to 33 out of 100, citing the coup and institutional collapse. On July 10, 2026, former prime minister and opposition leader Domingos Simoes Pereira was ordered back to prison; on July 21, ECOWAS demanded the release of all detained political figures. A review triggered by these events proposed a lower score of 13.1, which would cross Guinea-Bissau into the Critical band. The published 20.3 had never been individually reviewed before and predates the coup, so this proposal reflects the military government's own actions rather than a data-quality artifact. It has not been applied.

evidence.quote: a military coup in late 2025 thwarted efforts to restore regular political order by holding overdue elections
evidence.source: Freedom House, Freedom in the World 2026

evidence.quote: The West African bloc ECOWAS has urged Guinea-Bissau's military-led government to unconditionally release all detained political figures.
Pereira was one of several politicians jailed by the military after it seized power in November last year, replacing President Umaro Sissoco Embalo.

topSignals.title: A Math Error, Not a Conduct Problem, Is Found in Becton Dickinson's Public Score
topSignals.whyItMatters: A company's posted score did not match its own underlying data. Fixing an arithmetic mistake like this is bookkeeping, not a verdict on how the company is treating patients or workers this month.
topSignals.description: Becton Dickinson's published score remains 54.1 out of 100, in the Functional band. A review found that this number does not add up correctly from Becton Dickinson's own eight underlying category scores, which produce 42.2 under the benchmark's standard formula, an 11.9-point gap confirmed by the benchmark's own data-checking tool. The category scores themselves are unchanged; only the combined total was wrong. A July 9, 2026 FDA alert on Becton Dickinson's recall of more than 970 lots of ChloraPrep and FREPP surgical-prep applicators, prompted by wrinkled packaging that risked contamination, is a single data point consistent with the existing scores, not the cause of the 11.9-point gap. Becton Dickinson stays in the Functional band under both the old and the corrected number. The correction has not been applied to the public score.

evidence.quote: FDA shares Medline's recall of more than 970 lots of convenience kits

topSignals.title: Congo's Ebola Outbreak Passes 1,000 Deaths in Under Ten Weeks, the Fastest Pace on Record
topSignals.whyItMatters: A near-bottom score for the Democratic Republic of the Congo held steady, not because nothing is wrong, but because a record-fast epidemic confirms a capacity gap the score already reflected.
topSignals.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's score held near the bottom of the scale at 1.3 out of 100, close to its published 2.3. By July 23, 2026, the country's Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak had reached 1,033 deaths and 2,536 cases, crossing 1,000 deaths faster than any Ebola outbreak on record. The outbreak is spreading amid ongoing armed conflict, which this review found compounds rather than excuses the state's inability to contain it. No evidence of effective containment or reform was found this cycle, so the near-floor score was confirmed rather than lowered further.

evidence.quote: The DRC's Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak reached 1,033 deaths / 2,536 cases as of Jul 23, having crossed 1,000 deaths faster than any prior recorded Ebola outbreak.

topSignals.title: Russia and Iran Hold Near the Bottom of the Scale for Their Own Conduct; Ukraine and Palestine Hold Steady Despite Rising Attacks Against Them
topSignals.whyItMatters: This benchmark scores what a government does, not what is done to it. Being attacked does not lower a score; only a government's own actions do, and that rule was tested across six countries at once tonight.
topSignals.description: Russia and Israel both held at the benchmark's absolute floor of 0 out of 100. A UN report attributed a 37 percent rise in Ukrainian civilian casualties to escalating Russian long-range strikes, which is Russia's own conduct and confirms its floor score. Iran's score held near the floor at 2.5 after Iranian strikes hit a Kuwaiti desalination and power plant, killing a civilian, and a Jordanian air base, in July 2026 -- also Russia and Iran's own actions. By contrast, Ukraine's score held at 50 and Palestine's held at 25, even though both face rising casualties, because that harm is being done to them by others rather than by their own governments. Gaza's post-ceasefire death toll reached 1,185 as of July 23, and OCHA documented new displacement and shelter-aid shortfalls in the Palestinian territories, but under the benchmark's rules, harm inflicted on a population does not by itself lower that population's own government's score.

evidence.claim: A UN report attributed a 37 percent rise in Ukrainian civilian casualties to escalating Russian long-range strikes on Ukrainian cities.
Israeli strikes and shootings continued almost daily in Gaza despite the October 2025 ceasefire, with the cumulative toll reaching 1,185 killed and 3,816 wounded as of July 23.

topSignals.title: Flash Flooding Paralyzes Ahmedabad, India, but the City's Score Reflects a Longer Pattern
topSignals.whyItMatters: One extreme storm is a single data point. Ahmedabad's low score reflects thin, reactive disaster planning built up over time, not this one flood.
topSignals.description: Ahmedabad's score held at 18.8 out of 100, in the Critical band. On July 23-24, 2026, 177 millimeters of rain fell in two hours, prompting a red alert, school and college closures, and more than 100 cancelled trains. Separately, after a fatal firecracker-factory explosion, the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation inspected 300 units in a two-day fire-safety enforcement drive -- a response this review found reactive rather than a sign of sustained proactive inspection. Both events were weighed against the city's broader 40-part record rather than treated as the whole score, and the published score was confirmed.

evidence.claim: 177 millimeters of rain fell on Ahmedabad in two hours on July 23-24, 2026, prompting a red alert, school and college closures, and more than 100 cancelled trains.

topSignals.title: New York Sues DuPont Over 'Forever Chemicals' in Everyday Products
topSignals.whyItMatters: A new state lawsuit over long-lasting industrial chemicals adds one more data point to a company's already-known liability history; it confirms rather than resets DuPont's score.
topSignals.description: DuPont's score held at 29.4 out of 100, close to its published 29.7, in the Developing band. On July 9, 2026, New York's attorney general sued DuPont, along with 3M, Chemours, and Corteva, alleging the companies knowingly sold PFAS-containing "forever chemicals" in consumer products despite known links to cancer and developmental harm. The suit seeks cleanup funding and consumer warnings. These allegations have not yet been decided in court. This review found the suit reinforces, rather than newly establishes, DuPont's existing weak Awareness and Accountability scores, which already reflect a long PFAS liability history, so the published score was confirmed.

evidence.claim: New York's Attorney General sued 3M, DuPont, Chemours, and Corteva, alleging they knowingly sold harmful PFAS "forever chemicals" in consumer goods despite known cancer and developmental-harm links.

methodologyNotes.name: A Data Correction Is Not the Same as a Conduct Finding
methodologyNotes.description: Sometimes a company's or country's posted score does not match its own underlying category scores when added up using the benchmark's standard formula. When that happens, the fix is to correct the arithmetic, not to treat it as new evidence about how the entity is behaving. Becton Dickinson's proposed correction this cycle -- from 54.1 to 42.2 -- is exactly this kind of fix: its eight category scores are unchanged, only the combined total was wrong. The company stays in the same Functional band either way.

methodologyNotes.name: Conduct Is Scored, Not Victimhood
methodologyNotes.description: The benchmark scores what a government or company does, not what happens to it. Tonight, Russia's and Iran's scores held near the bottom of the scale because of their own strikes on civilian infrastructure. Ukraine's and Palestine's scores held steady despite rising casualties, because that harm was inflicted on them by others, not caused by their own governments. The same rule applied to Israel, whose floor score was confirmed by its own continuing conduct rather than by what is happening in the region generally.

methodologyNotes.name: A Coup Can Move a Score Fast When the Evidence Is the Government's Own Conduct
methodologyNotes.description: Most large proposed score changes trace back to a flat, untested starting estimate meeting its first real review, not to new bad conduct. Guinea-Bissau's proposed downgrade this cycle is different: its published score predates the November 2025 coup entirely, and the proposed lower score reflects the military government's own actions since then -- jailing the opposition leader and triggering suspension from three regional and international bodies. That is a genuine conduct-driven proposal, not an arithmetic artifact, even though it has not yet been applied.
